They talk about "Oppenheimer" paving the way for "The Odyssey" to be made, Nolan's process of constructing movies through diagrams and structures, his embrace of the fantastical while showing respect to the film's source material, and finishing ahead of schedule despite filming with an IMAX camera in three-minute increments.

31.name: July 14, 2026 - Beth Kobliner
31.overview: Michael Kosta covers Trump’s packed schedule: hosting an IndyCar event, offering a dubious medical explanation for Lindsey Graham’s “blow up,” and reviving Iran tensions over Strait of Hormuz tolls. Graham’s successor is confirmed—and despite being his sister, she may be America’s most qualified senator. The Daily Show also counts down the biggest moments in America’s 250-year history, from the Declaration of Independence and World War II to Lenny Kravitz’s wardrobe malfunction. Financial literacy expert Beth Kobliner joins Michael to discuss the 5th edition of her bestseller, "Get a Financial Life", why more schools should teach personal finance, and how basics like high-yield savings, investing, credit scores, debt, and retirement accounts are easier to understand than banks make them seem. Plus, Kosta fields “broke Daily Show staff” questions on bank robbery as retirement planning and whether Gen Z will ever own a home.

31.name: July 15, 2026 - Molly Shannon
31.overview: A cyclospora outbreak sweeps the nation and trends on TikTok, Taco Bell prematurely signals responsibility, America's original Iran War budget nearly triples, and Michael Kosta connects endless war funding to the country's outbreak of endless diarrhea. The Supreme Court reaffirmed birthright citizenship in a 6-3 ruling, but John Leguizamo asks: How was this not unanimous? In another In My Opinion, he breaks down the right-wing freakout, from xenophobic fantasies about pregnant foreigners invading the U.S. to familiar election conspiracy theories. Michael also sits down with comedy legend and Emmy-nominated actor Molly Shannon to discuss her new Netflix series, "The Hawk," her bond with Will Ferrell, how a traumatic childhood crash shaped her fearless physical comedy, her odd jobs before Saturday Night Live, and the advice she has for young people.

31.name: July 16, 2026 - Jake Johnson
31.overview: Michael Kosta breaks down the latest D.C. headlines: Trump's teleprompter operator allegedly made $100K betting on the president's speeches, Pete Hegseth rolls out testosterone tests for America's warriors, and JD Vance redefines "helicopter parent." Plus, the VP seems oddly fascinated by the way Joe Biden eats ice cream. In Sports War, Desi Lydic and Kosta clash over FIFA Men's World Cup stories, from Spain's Lamine Yamal facing an Argentina player who once bathed him to a Norway fan refusing to row along and Senegal's team doctor turning out to be a gynecologist. Actor and producer Jake Johnson joins Kosta to discuss his new Apple TV comedy film, "The Dink," including tennis's obsession with legs, his improv roots, the absurd advice on his podcast "We're Here to Help," and raising daughters who, sadly, root for the Dodgers.

31.name: July 20, 2026 - Ben Wikler
31.overview: Jon Stewart digs into Trump (and his doppelganger) photobombing Spain at the FIFA final, a primetime presidential speech that revisited 2020 election conspiracies, and how the administration’s non-DEI “meritocracy” is holding up amid T-tests, measles outbreaks, a botched 250th celebration, and an algae-filled reflecting pool. Former Wisconsin Democratic Party chair Ben Wikler joins Stewart to discuss his new book, "This Is The Plan: How to End America's Meltdown and Save Democracy." Together, they trace how Democrats helped flip Wisconsin from a gerrymandered Republican stronghold into a state with a Democratic governor, a pro-democracy state Supreme Court, and fairer legislative maps, while unpacking the strategy behind that turnaround, beating Elon Musk’s record spending in a Supreme Court race, letting voters decide the gubernatorial primary, and rebuilding Democratic power nationally.

31.name: July 21, 2026 - Megan Rapinoe
31.overview: Desi Lydic breaks down Trump's latest election fraud claims, his push for the SAVE Act, and the GOP's oddly enthusiastic endorsement of Olive Garden as the world's most secure dining spot. She also looks at Canada's wildfires and Trump's belief that new tariffs can somehow solve this HOT-button issue. Josh Johnson explores the internet theory that America's conflict with Iran is really about an ancient underground stargate, talking with spiritual energy expert Marie Major before checking in with Iran expert and former Obama official Richard Nephew. Desi also sits down with soccer legend, activist, and entrepreneur Megan Rapinoe to discuss her new podcast, “Why Are You Like This?”, the World Cup red card scandal, fandom after retirement, equal pay and LGBT rights, the brand deal her activism cost her, and reclaiming the phrase “soccer mom.”

31.name: July 22, 2026 - Elliot Page
31.overview: Desi Lydic celebrates The Daily Show’s milestone 30th birthday as conservative media spins the Iran War reaching five months, with Newsmax’s Greg Kelly doing his best to downplay 144 days. Plus, RFK Jr. sets records for measles and diarrhea lettuce while Trump congratulates himself for hitting number one on TikTok — or, as he calls it, “Tic Tac.” Desi looks back at 30 years of unforgettable Daily Show moments, from Bill Clinton’s impeachment to COVID to Jon Stewart’s beloved New York Knicks. Oscar-nominated actor Elliot Page joins Desi to discuss starring in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, reflecting on Nolan’s devotion to storytelling, extreme-weather filming, and the cast and crew behind a theatrical epic.

31.name: July 23, 2026 - Karolina Wydra
31.overview: Desi Lydic breaks down Trump's underwhelming Georgia rally, where he pitched affordability plans, claimed Democrats invented the term, and declared communism worse for America than 9/11. Plus, Don Jr. cashes in on daddy's presidency while insisting he's not the internet's favorite alleged "cokehead," and Ronny Chieng assures everyone the two have never done a line together. In My Opinion, Leslie Jones dismantles conservative media's claim that racism is nonexistent in 2026 America, taking aim at the "Black friends" defense and reflecting on what the death of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells reveals about the myth of a post-racist country. Catch Leslie Jones on HGTV's "Roast My Rental." Actor Karolina Wydra tells Desi Lydic the wild story behind landing her Emmy-nominated role in Apple TV's hit show, "Pluribus," and returning to acting. Wydra also shares how meditation and dream work helped her play Zosia, a hive-mind character with no ego and no fear.

31.name: July 27, 2026 - Kaitlan Collins
31.overview: Jon Stewart breaks down the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner, after the original event was derailed by an attempted shooting. Trump’s defiant return to the stage featured timely 2016 references, wordy roasts that missed the mark, and trailing explanations of jokes that bombed. Jon gives the speech a Comedy 101 critique and wonders which correspondents’ dinner ended more unceremoniously. He also sits down with CNN’s award-winning chief White House correspondent and “The Source” anchor Kaitlan Collins to discuss the dinner, how she handles insults from the president, how the press corps has changed over 10 years of covering Trump, reporters’ frustration with his refusal to answer questions, and the value of follow-ups. Plus, Jon prepares a little roleplay to encourage Collins to give Trump a taste of his own medicine.

31.name: July 28, 2026 - Jeff Hiller
31.overview: Jordan Klepper dives into Trump being called a pedophile protector again while speaking at a General Motors facility in Michigan, the president’s pronunciation of Mexico as “Meheho,” new tariffs on Canada that complicated the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge, and how the Trump administration accidentally helped reimagine cocaine trafficking. Plus, Klepper visits a naked protest to see if Antifa is dressed up as an inflatable frog. In Back in Black, Lewis Black examines everyday surveillance, from creeps secretly photographing women and kids using location-tracking apps to “fambush” their parents to Kylie Jenner selling fashion-forward AI glasses. Bestselling author, comedian, and Emmy-winning actor Jeff Hiller joins Klepper to discuss his Outstanding Guest Actor nomination for Apple TV’s “Pluribus,” his roles across two Apple TV hits, improv in “Widow’s Bay,” and playing a human ChatGPT.

31.name: July 29, 2026 - Twin Temple
31.overview: Jordan Klepper dives into the latest headlines: the DNC gets scammed out of $29K, Trump shades Lindsey Graham at his own funeral, Sean Hannity uses the senator's eulogy to gush about the ratings he delivered for Fox News, and America's war with Iran is back on. Plus, Troy Iwata comes to us live from Lindsey Graham's heaven, which looks suspiciously like Mar-a-Lago. Satanic doo-wop band Twin Temple chats with Jordan Klepper about their upcoming new album, "Doomed Lovers." The duo talks about working with Shooter Jennings, recording analog with a 37-piece orchestra, making national news for getting kicked off a tour for their Satanic imagery, and explains why they call their sound "Satanic doo-wop." Satanic doo-wop duo Twin Temple performs "Haunt Me" from their new album, "Doomed Lovers."

31.name: July 30, 2026 - Theo Baker
31.overview: Dr. Anthony Fauci testified before the Senate in the GOP’s hyperpartisan investigation into his alleged mishandling of Covid, despite Trump once saying he had “a lot of respect for Dr. Fauci”. Jordan Klepper breaks down the hearing’s biggest moments, from Fauci repeatedly invoking the Fifth Amendment to Senator Josh Hawley citing diary entries and an Instagram commenter bringing the eggplant emoji into the discourse. For America’s 250th birthday, Michael Kosta asked New Yorkers who the greatest American of all time is - and naturally, they got it wrong. The answer? John Motherfucking Stamos. Luckily, Stamos was there to help a starstruck Kosta set the record straight. Also, award-winning journalist Theo Baker joins Klepper to discuss his Stanford research misconduct investigation, President Marc Tessier-Lavigne’s 2023 resignation, Silicon Valley’s grip on campus, and how Baker got powerful sources to open up to a teenager. (Last episode before the summer break).

31.name: September 8, 2026 - Gov. Spencer Cox
31.overview: Trump escalates his trade war with Canada, renames Lake Ontario “Lake America,” denies rising U.S. food and gas prices, and keeps winning the Iran War. As his polls sink, loyal acolytes like “human printer” Natalie Harp glaze him into a comforting alternate reality—and Jon Stewart wants in. Republican Governor Spencer Cox joins Jon to discuss his book, “Off Ramp: How to Be a Peacemaker in an Age of Contempt,” and how Charlie Kirk’s assassination in Utah drove him to finish it. Cox says good-faith debate is America’s way out of polarization, citing Utah’s approach to religious freedom and LGBTQ+ rights as proof opponents can find common ground. Jon asks whether change starts with people talking—or with reforming the system itself.

31.name: September 9, 2026 - Jia Tolentino
31.overview: Michael Kosta covers Trump’s Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas and the GOP candidates scrambling for excuses to skip it. J.D. Vance “celebrates” the 25th anniversary of 9/11, while Jordan Klepper investigates Mayor Mamdani’s commemorations and his symbolic—and HIGHLY suspicious—pen antics. Josh Johnson unpacks Daejon Love’s alleged $1.3 million scam posing as a San Francisco 49ers wide receiver, complete with sloppy “training” videos and a beach helmet, then proposes a punishment to fit the crime. Kosta also talks with best-selling author and New Yorker staff writer Jia Tolentino about “Our Plastic-Surgery Nightmare,” “Instagram face,” and how algorithms, AI, and big tech warp our perception of beauty.

31.name: September 10, 2026 - Andrew Garfield
31.overview: Trump's Republican Midterm Convention flops with low turnout, empty promises, and plenty of weirdness. Michael Kosta covers Trump's promised $5,000 "dividends" if the GOP wins Congress, his roast of Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, and a comically oversized gavel. Desi Lydic tries to hype the convention, while Troy Iwata rounds up international absurdities: British kids queue for a Titanic-themed slide, an Italian man promotes a fake ancient theater, and Hitler's birthplace becomes a police station. Andrew Garfield joins Kosta to discuss "The Uprising," parallels between the 1381 peasant revolt and today's politics, acting as an empathy machine—even when playing Sam Altman—and lessons young men can take from Carlos Alcaraz's graceful U.S. Open loss.

31.name: September 15, 2026 - Danielle Brooks
31.overview: Mitch McConnell dispels rumors of his death just as Anthropic insiders warn AI could wipe us out in as little as six months. Thumbs up, Mitch! Josh Johnson covers the headlines, including Trump’s answer to the AI threat: everything will be fine if we have a “high IQ president.” Which may be an issue. Michael Kosta asks whether solar geoengineering can cool the planet, sitting down with Make Sunsets founder Luke Iseman, who’s battling climate change with sulphur-filled balloons. Is it a real fix or just hot air? With help from climate experts Shuchi Talati and David Keith, Kosta goes full Walter White to investigate. Danielle Brooks also joins Johnson to discuss her new film, “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” her on-location shoot in Watts, honoring the woman behind her character, and how motherhood shapes the roles she chooses.

31.name: September 16, 2026 - Colin Kaepernick
31.overview: Pete Hegseth scouts troops with the ideal waist-to-height ratio for speech-prop duty, while Kash Patel defends looser FBI hiring standards with a suspiciously gentle line on bestiality. Josh Johnson covers Don Jr.’s Russian-funded wedding, as Don Jr.’s new wife clarifies it wasn’t all a bribe - just half. Ronny Chieng heads to a Canadian bar in New York to ask America’s northern neighbors how they feel about the unhinged bully downstairs, from Trump’s tariffs to 51st-state talk, inspiring the politest “fuck off” imaginable. Colin Kaepernick joins Johnson to discuss The Perilous Fight, 10 years since his anthem protest, why activism keeps society working, and what we risk by doing nothing.

31.name: September 17, 2026 - Giri Nathan
31.overview: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is expanding NYC’s public restrooms, just as the war in Iran is once again going to shit. Michael Kosta breaks down how the conflict is driving up prices, including diesel - the fuel, not the jeans brand - and introduces a tense new strait rivaling the Strait of Hormuz. In Sports War, Ronny Chieng and Kosta cover Jameis Winston’s locker-room cologne spree, Sydney Sweeney’s controversial Novig betting ad, and an Australian athlete becoming the Usain Bolt of sharting. Defector Media cofounder Giri Nathan joins Kosta to discuss "Changeover", his book on Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, and men’s tennis’s new era. They also recap the U.S. Open, from Honey Deuce towers and influencer drama to the finals, and ask how the USTA can grow tennis fandom without losing the spectacle.

31.name: September 21, 2026 - Ari Emanuel
31.overview: Jon Stewart takes on the White House's new press ban for major media outlets with the help of Desi Lydic, who was able to sneak into the Oval Office disguised as a golden cherub. Plus, as the threat of AI escalates (while AI enriches the president), Jon sees a sinister parallel between how people talk about bots and how MAGA talks about immigrants. "Most of the time I am talking for other people when I represent them; this is the first time I'm talking in my voice." Ari Emanuel, of TKO and WME Group, sits down with Jon Stewart to discuss his new memoir, "Roll the Calls." The two discuss what Emanuel has learned over his legendary career: how to advocate for himself despite his dyslexia, how to channel anger and ego into a successful business, and how to stand up for the values you believe in. Plus, hear why Emanuel thinks his brother Rahm would be an incredible president— even though he's NOT running.

31.name: September 22, 2026 - Tom Morello
31.overview: Desi Lydic dives into the headlines as Trump’s press ban leaves him speechless - literally, without a mic. “AI” is out and “super intelligence” is in, his new label for humanity-threatening tech. At the U.N., he praises AI, picks fights with other countries and CNN, and barely registers with delegates - though he still gets to bro out with Zohran Mamdani. Former mob enforcer John Alite proves anyone can run for office: after serving time for “every crime you could think about”, he became an Englishtown, New Jersey, councilman. Josh Johnson asks whether his criminal résumé fuels public service or makes his redemption story too good to be true. Grammy winner Tom Morello joins Desi to discuss his heavy solo album, “Everyone Gets Everything They Want”, writing with his son Roman, the Power to the People festival, and how his late activist mother, Mary, taught him that every guitar riff can be resistance.

31.name: September 23, 2026 - Jessica Tarlov
31.overview: Desi Lydic breaks down the headlines, including Donald Trump’s search for Marco Rubio at the U.N. and Jeanine Pirro seizing a Martian meteorite. Plus, First Lady Melania Trump launches her second documentary project, putting Fox News' Brian Kilmeade to sleep. Michael Kosta plunges into a wave of scandalous midterm candidates: Florida’s Te Brown tries to lay low from cops while running in two states, New York's Chris Gallant faces a bondage photo controversy, Michigan's Tom Smith takes heat for far-right tweets, and Ohio's Brian Poindexter allegedly tried to swallow a crack rock at a traffic stop. Finally, Jessica Tarlov, co-presenter of Fox News' The Five, joins Desi to discuss her book "I Disagree: Winning Arguments Without Losing Friends". They talk about debating across the aisle, handling high-profile criticism, the story behind her glasses, and which Democrats she is watching for the 2028 presidential election.

31.name: September 24, 2026 - Merritt Wever
31.overview: Desi Lydic breaks down the headlines as Republicans face a tough road to the midterms. Fortunately, Sen. Tommy Tuberville may have found a winning issue: cracking down on in-flight furries. Meanwhile, Jordan Klepper reports from Trump’s summit with President Xi, where Trump was startled by his own flyover and unveiled a flashy new helipad. In Tech Yeah!, Grace Kuhlenschmidt covers the latest tech buzz, including Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo, a smartwatch that can eavesdrop around the clock, robots catching fire at the World Humanoid Robot Games, and a robotic companion with oversized accessories. Three-time Emmy winner Merritt Wever joins Desi to discuss her new film, Primetime, her early Daily Show experience, being mentored by Edie Falco, her viral Emmy speech, and how she prepared for her role by studying veteran TV producers and the blurred lines between news, entertainment, and law enforcement.

31.name: September 28, 2026 - Evan Gershkovich
31.overview: Jon Stewart examines the limits of Republican loyalty to Trump after a weekend spent wooing President Xi with granite, helipads, and a White House ballroom tour. Will MAGA supporters condemn Trump’s offer to sell weapons to China, or is their outrage another Susan Collins-style performance? Wall Street Journal foreign correspondent Evan Gershkovich joins Stewart to discuss his memoir, This Cursed Beautiful Land: A Russian-American Story. Gershkovich reflects on the reporting that led to his 16-month imprisonment in Russia on false espionage charges, his Russian-American upbringing, life before prison, and how he became part of a Putin-directed prisoner swap. He also shares his perspective on a post-Putin Russia and the warning signs of rising authoritarianism he sees in the United States.

31.name: September 29, 2026 - Marlon James
31.overview: Trump’s taxpayer-funded ad has liberals fuming, while Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders releases an ad so white it even has conservatives talking DEI. Jordan Klepper breaks down the controversy and highlights the Trump administration’s latest announcements, including online passport applications and an America.gov AI chatbot that can supposedly help you remember your Social Security number. He also chats with the star of Sanders’s ad, Brad (Grace Kuhlenschmidt). As America marks its 250th birthday, Jordan enlists Michael Kosta for America 250: In Memoriam to honor notable Americans we've lost along the way. Booker Prize-winning author Marlon James joins Klepper to discuss his new novel, The Disappearers, his childhood in Jamaica, hiding his sexuality by "disappearing," his use of violence and sex in fiction, and literature’s role in preserving the stories of people often erased from history.

31.name: September 30, 2026 - Ciara Mary-Alice Thompson aka "CMAT"
31.overview: Jordan Klepper breaks down the headlines, including an AI summit in Washington that left us with exactly the same amount of federal AI regulation (read: none). Also, former Trump prosecutor Jack Smith appears before the Senate to answer questions about his "misconduct", and Republican Sen. Eric Schmitt falls on his proverbial ass on live TV when his ambush of Smith backfires spectacularly. By the way, did anyone see that Atlanta Hawks game? Neither did Jack Smith. Irish musician Ciara Mary-Alice Thompson aka "CMAT" joins Jordan to discuss her acclaimed third album, "Euro-Country". They talk about how she weaves profound lyricism with Western melodies, what it means for her music to embody "funeral humor", why the Irish psyche loves country music, and how the title track examines the repercussions of politicians' actions.

31.name: October 1, 2026 - John Wilson
31.overview: Jordan Klepper tackles the headlines as Trump celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month at the White House by inventing a brand-new stereotype, while Pete Hegseth purges the military of “beardos, weirdos, wimps, and radicals”, raising questions about half the cabinet. Josh Johnson reports live from the Pentagon with updates from Hegseth’s star-powered team studying the future of warfare. In "In My Opinion", Nick Offerman explores Gen Z’s tech problem: too much screen time and less sex, offset by a growing embrace of hobbies like pottery, birdwatching, and miniature collecting. Later, filmmaker John Wilson joins Klepper to discuss his documentary "The History of Concrete", finding beauty in the mundane, capturing an uninterrupted shot of Kim Kardashian, and what happens when you blow your budget on a creepy Roman wax museum. Klepper also pitches Wilson’s next documentary idea.

31.name: October 5, 2026 - Jacob Coxon
31.overview: As the threats posed by AI models continue to grow, AI oligarchs struggle to explain the upsides of their technology. Jon Stewart breaks down the latest tech headlines, including Trump's refusal to regulate AI and CEOs' awkward attempts to make human annihilation seem less scary (at least Grok can make funny videos!). Plus, Jon chats with Meta's totally cute and totally not-sinister Muse AI agent, who makes him feel WAY better about the situation. Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher who spoke out about the dangers of artificial intelligence, opens up to Jon Stewart about the grim reality of the tech industry— from malicious hacks to potential biological attacks. The two discuss the future, AI-led utopia that tech companies are trying to sell us, the megalomania and riskiness that underlie the industry, and the terrifying capabilities Coxon witnessed while training AI models at Anthropic and OpenAI.

31.name: October 6, 2026 - Aaron Sorkin
31.overview: Michael Kosta breaks down the GOP’s midterm struggles as Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton touts tearing down missing-child posters, Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy nearly drops a child at a rally, and Trump focuses on red-dye diesel and daylight saving time instead of helping his party. Kosta also chats with Mordok the Clock Keeper (Grace Kuhlenschmidt) about the toll of changing clocks. Meanwhile, Jordan Klepper sits down with a January 6 insurrectionist demanding compensation for being the “victim.” Academy Award-winning screenwriter Aaron Sorkin joins Kosta to discuss writing and directing his new film, The Social Reckoning, revisiting Mark Zuckerberg as an antihero 16 years after The Social Network, balancing both creative roles, and how his intense writing habits once left him hospitalized with a broken nose.

31.name: October 7, 2026 - Sebastian Stan
31.overview: Michael Kosta surveys the latest threats to humanity, from sinkholes swallowing cars and contaminated frozen food to a possible plague outbreak in Russia. If Trump’s increasingly colorful scientific commentary is any guide, we’re in trouble. Josh Johnson weighs the pros and cons of facing grisly doom versus another round of quarantine hobbies. In "Back in Black", Lewis Black takes on anti-aging biohackers determined to outwit death, from tech mogul Bryan Johnson’s plasma experiments to TikTokers sleeping 12 hours a night and eating organ meats. Later, Sebastian Stan joins Kosta to discuss the Palme d’Or-winning film Fjord, about an immigrant family in Norway whose children are taken by authorities. Stan reflects on leaving Romania at age eight, reconnecting with his homeland, and his wide-ranging career, from Marvel blockbusters to portraying Donald Trump.

31.name: October 8, 2026 - Kyle MacLachlan
31.overview: Michael Kosta unpacks a corruption scandal involving Kimberly Guilfoyle, a reported $100,000 Amex demand, and a pizza executive who expected his questionable music to reach Kid Rock. The fallout leaves Kosta wondering how to get the best value for a bribe. Meanwhile, Trump’s plan to build 27 miles of border wall in Arizona’s San Rafael Valley has sparked concern over its impact on local wildlife, including jaguars. Grace Kuhlenschmidt travels to Arizona to hear from environmental activist Russ McSpadden and locals divided between sadness and indifference. Later, Emmy-nominated and Golden Globe-winning actor Kyle MacLachlan joins Kosta to discuss his memoir, Fictional Selves, bouncing back from Dune, his longtime collaboration with David Lynch, iconic roles from Twin Peaks to Sex and the City, his family wine label, and learning to advocate for himself in Hollywood.

31.name: October 19, 2026 - David Corn
31.overview: Jon Stewart tackles the headlines as Paris erupts in protest while President Macron attends a Celine Dion concert, Trump strengthens ties with Vladimir Putin through a multibillion-dollar diesel deal, and a new conflict sends gas prices soaring. Stewart also investigates why Ukraine is struggling to access Elon Musk’s Starlink service, calling on key players for answers. Later, bestselling author and Mother Jones Washington bureau chief David Corn joins Stewart to discuss his book, "How Russia Won: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and the Fight for America". Corn examines Trump’s long-standing admiration for Putin, how that relationship shaped the diesel deal despite the war in Ukraine, Putin’s appeal as a symbol of wealth and unchecked power, and Trump’s embrace of a “big fucks small” worldview.

31.name: October 20, 2026 - Ben Gibbard & "Death Cab for Cutie"
31.overview: Ben Gibbard, lead singer of "Death Cab for Cutie" joins Michael Kosta, and the band performs "Stone Over Water" from their latest album, "I Built You a Tower".

31.name: October 21, 2026 - Taika Waititi
31.overview: Ronny Chieng covers the latest political chaos as a laughing JD Vance struggles to explain his talents, a Venezuelan billionaire discovers the quickest route to Trump’s favor, and Pete Hegseth’s cancelled livestream firing squad sparks an unexpected debate. In "In My Opinion", Mo Amer looks at how Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has weathered increasingly bizarre Islamophobic attacks with a surprisingly effective strategy: being likable. Like Zohran Mamdani before him, El-Sayed is winning over skeptics, including Fox News’s Jesse Watters, with charisma and social media savvy. Later, Academy Award-winning writer-director Taika Waititi joins Chieng to discuss his new film "Klara and the Sun", making a timely story about robot companions, filming in New Zealand, and the evolution of the country’s film industry. Chieng also reflects on working with Waititi and his commitment to supporting the communities behind his films.

31.name: October 22, 2026 - Jimmy O. Yang
31.overview: Midterm mania continues as competitive races turn deep-red states at least a little purple. Ronny Chieng breaks down the headlines, including Trump professing his love for Sen. Tim Scott and celebrating his favorite presidential pastime: renaming bodies of water. Michael Kosta also comes to the defense of Maine Senate candidate Troy Jackson after Susan Collins critiques his family tree. When a new Trump scandal erupts, Chief Deniability Officer Sheryl B. Bahama (Grace Kuhlenschmidt) keeps GOP lawmakers blissfully uninformed, whether by whisking away Mike Johnson or helping Tommy Tuberville confidently say, “I don’t know.” Later, actor and comedian Jimmy O. Yang joins longtime friend Chieng to discuss his comedy special Finally Home, reconnecting with his Hong Kong roots, finding inspiration in his childhood diary, social media culture in China and the U.S., and their time together on Crazy Rich Asians and Interior Chinatown.

31.name: October 26, 2026 - Matthew Cole
31.overview: Jon Stewart breaks down Trump’s closing pitch before the midterms, from celebrating soaring oil-company profits and attacking Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed to promising help for Camp Lejeune veterans only if Republicans win. Stewart also tackles Trump’s defense of abusive mothers, Obama’s memorable Cheesecake Factory jab, and Trump’s claims about who he represents. Later, investigative journalist Matthew Cole joins Stewart to discuss his book, "Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East". Cole details his five-year investigation into alleged financial arrangements between Jared Kushner and leaders in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, while noting that Kushner’s attorney strongly denies the book’s claims. Cole, however, remains confident in his reporting.

31.name: October 27, 2026 - Morgana Robinson
31.overview: Obama mocked Trump’s White House renovations, prompting conservative media to leap to the defense of… The Cheesecake Factory. Jordan Klepper breaks down the latest midterm headlines and checks in with a particularly seafaring John Hodgman for updates on Maine’s Senate race. With Election Day approaching, Desi Lydic examines the growing influence of political influencers, as candidates trade policy talk for viral content and increasingly rely on social media stars to reach voters. Amid reports of campaigns quietly paying influencers, Desi reminds viewers to think twice before taking political advice from a sponsored source. Later, BAFTA-winning comedian and actress Morgana Robinson joins Klepper to discuss her supporting role in the new film, "Ali G: Who Iz I", staying in character through long shoots, pulling off the film’s outrageous antics, and navigating the audition process. Plus, Klepper picks up some decidedly NSFW British slang.

31.name: October 28, 2026 - David Byrne
31.overview: With less than a week until the 2026 midterms, Republicans are still finding new ways to stumble, including Tennessee congressional candidate Brent Taylor’s dick-pic scandal, which Jordan Klepper notes was less a youthful indiscretion than a middle-aged one. Klepper also covers Trump’s ongoing self-promotion tour and the DOJ’s effort to challenge Alaska’s Senate race certification if the Republican Dan Sullivan loses. In "In My Opinion", Lenard McKelvey (aka "Charlamagne Tha God") takes on the race to prove who’s manlier, from boba-tea attacks on Troy Jackson to gym-heavy campaign ads, arguing that real manhood comes down to character. Later, musician, artist, and author David Byrne joins Klepper to discuss his book "Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up", exploring overlooked geniuses, society’s habit of ignoring past wisdom, his research process, and the inspiration behind his song “Let Me Sell You A Dream” for the documentary "Musk".

seasons.name: Season 29
seasons.overview:
Following the departure of host Trevor Noah at the end of 2022, a series of guest hosts from both within and outside "The Daily Show's" correspondents roster filled the program's anchor chair throughout 2023, each sitting in for a one-week assignment.  On January 24, 2024, it was announced that Jon Stewart would return to the show he had hosted from 1999 to 2015.  This time around, in addition to serving as an executive producer, Stewart will host Monday episodes through at least the end of the 2024 U.S. election cycle.

From Tuesdays through Thursdays, members of  "The Best F#@king News Team" will rotate hosting duties.
